newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 7-yr coupon rate falls to 13.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 7-yr coupon rate falls to 13.5 pct.

text.p: The coupon rate on the Philippine seven-year, fixed rate Treasury bond on Tuesday tumbled to 13.5 percent from 14.0 percent in the previous auction held in December 1996, the Bureau of Treasury said.
Market response to the auction, however, was tepid as it attracted only 3.34 billion pesos worth of tenders, all of which were accepted.
The government had planned to sell 3.5 billion pesos worth of the T-bonds.
"There's no interest from the market. The rate was too low," a foreign bank dealer said.
Bidders just priced the T-bonds at a premium over the five-year T-bonds with a latest coupon rate of 12.5 percent, the dealer said.
The average rate amounted to 12.374 percent, with the low at 11.645 and the high at 13.5 percent.

Domestic interest rates had been on a decline since the one percentage point cut in reserve requirements early this year. A 20 percent tax on term reverse repos also led to the high liquidity in the market, dealers said.
